findings.evidence: Upstream analogue `upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Measure/CharacteristicFunction/Basic.lean:173` `lemma norm_charFun_le (t : E) : ‖charFun μ t‖ ≤ μ.real Set.univ` under ambient `{μ : Measure E}` (line 127, no finiteness instance). Both ingredients of the suggested proof are unconditional in Mathlib: `Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean:967` `theorem norm_integral_le_integral_norm (f : α → G) : ‖∫ a, f a ∂μ‖ ≤ ∫ a, ‖f a‖ ∂μ` and `Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean:987` `theorem integral_const (c : E) : ∫ _ : α, c ∂μ = μ.real univ • c` (whose proof has an explicit non-finite branch at lines 991-993). The finiteness enters only via `norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const` (`Integral/Bochner/Basic.lean:999`, `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]`), the lemma currently used.
findings.fix: Drop the instance: `theorem norm_anisotropyCoeff_le (μ : Measure (AddCircle T)) (n : ℤ) : ‖anisotropyCoeff μ n‖ ≤ μ.real Set.univ := by rw [anisotropyCoeff_def]; exact (norm_integral_le_integral_norm _).trans_eq (by simp [norm_fourier_eval])`. `norm_anisotropyCoeff_le_one` is unchanged.
findings.issue: `norm_anisotropyCoeff_le (μ : Measure (AddCircle T)) [IsFiniteMeasure μ] (n : ℤ) : ‖anisotropyCoeff μ n‖ ≤ μ.real Set.univ` assumes finiteness that the statement does not need. The adjacent `anisotropyCoeff_zero` (line 264) states the same quantity `μ.real Set.univ` with no instance, and `anisotropyCoeff_withDensity_eq_fourierCoeff_neg` (line 289) builds `haarAddCircle.withDensity f` with only ae-measurability and ae-finiteness of `f`, so the file itself produces measures to which the bound does not apply. (This refines, not reverses, the earlier round's finding: the general-bound/probability-corollary split stays; only the instance goes.)

summary: Statements sit at the natural level throughout (pairwise independence, arbitrary `Finset` and `NonAssocRing` in the off-diagonal file, `n : ℤ`, real forms derived from complex ones, no special-case duplication). One residual over-assumption: `norm_anisotropyCoeff_le` carries `[IsFiniteMeasure μ]` where the exact Mathlib analogue and the file's own neighbouring lemma carry none.
